A.name: Internal Otsu Body Extraction
A.principle: Apply Otsu threshold within the contour mask to separate object body (brighter) from shadow/background (darker)

B.name: Center-weighted Mask (distance transform)
B.principle: Weight pixels by distance from contour boundary — interior pixels get higher weight in color vote

blue_cup.note: center L=20 is dark cup body

C.name: Chroma Filtering (C = sqrt((A-128)^2+(B-128)^2))
C.principle: Exclude near-neutral pixels (C < 5) from color voting — only chromatic pixels participate

blue_block.note: good survival but black still dominates (color range mismatch)

blue_cup.note: 57% C<5, body B=111 in blue range

composite_strategy.recommended: Method A (Otsu) as base, then Method C (Chroma) on surviving body pixels
composite_strategy.rationale: Otsu removes shadow (class-agnostic), Chroma removes residual neutral pixels. Each filters a different noise source. Otsu catches dark leaks (background shadows), Chroma catches achromatic leaks (gray table pixels). Order matters: Otsu first because it removes the bulk of shadow; Chroma second on the cleaner body set.
composite_strategy.expected_gain: Reduces black pixel count by 20-60% across all cases while preserving >70% of genuine chromatic object pixels
